messages:
elena: heads-up — i'm opening a PR to consolidate the timeout, rate-limit, and context-trim troubleshooting notes into a single error-reference section. aiming to reduce duplication and surface clear fallback flows. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2345 :mage:
ryan: nice, thanks for doing this. quick ask — can we include a short decision flow (retry vs degrade vs fallback) for each error class? makes it easier for engs to pick a path quickly. :eyes:
priya: happy to add SDK snippets. which languages should we prioritize? js + python or add go/ruby too?
elena: js + python for the initial pass, please. smaller snippets only (<= 8 lines) so they fit the reference card. also want a tiny example showing handling of Retry-After and context trimming.
priya: got it. i'll add two snippets and a short note about exponential backoff + jitter.
carlos: small nit — use exponential backoff with capped jitter in examples. and include a note about avoiding tight loops when Retry-After is missing. i can draft the pseudo-code.
samira: link-check: there's an old playground example linked from the timeout doc that 404s. i'll put the replacement (/console/streams#resume) in the PR comments.
docs-bot: PR opened by elena: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2345 — CI: docs-lint passed, linkcheck flagged 1 broken link. Assigned reviewers: @ryan.
ryan: thanks. i'll scan wording and link sweep after lunch. one thing — do we keep the 'context-trim heuristics' in troubleshooting or move it under Optimize? i lean troubleshooting but cross-link to Optimize.
elena: agree — keep the practical heuristics in troubleshooting for quick triage, then a "for tuning" pointer to Optimize with deeper recommender logic.
priya: sample JS snippet for Retry-After handling (draft):
```js
// respect Retry-After header
const res = await client.generate(req)
if (res.status === 429) {
  const wait = parseInt(res.headers['retry-after'] || '1', 10)
  await sleep(wait * 1000)
  // then retry with backoff
}
```
priya: i'll replace the naive sleep with an exponential backoff helper before finalizing.
carlos: i'll add a pseudo-code example with jitter and a max retry cap. also include a short check for "out-of-context" (prompt length > model.limit) and suggest trimming older messages first.
elena: samira, can you embed the replacement link to the streaming-resume guide you mentioned? and please attach the slide with the small flowchart.
samira: done — slide here: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1XyZ-flowchart. i added a one-slide flow: 1) 429 -> read Retry-After, 2) if streaming interruption -> resume token, 3) if context > limit -> trim oldest.
elena: perfect. i'll update the PR with that embed and move the old playground link to a redirect. i'll also add a tiny table mapping: error -> quick-fix -> long-term fix.
ryan: sounds good. one more: include an explicit example for the SDK that demonstrates trimming conversation state before calling generate (so folks copy-paste it).
priya: adding that now. sample python context-trim snippet:
```py
# trim context to last N tokens/messages
while tokens(context) > model_limit - margin:
    context.pop(0)
resp = client.generate(context)
```
priya: will tidy and add comments before i push.
carlos: FYI, i'll send a small PR to normalize frontmatter so permalinks don't change when we merge.
elena: thank you all. plan: i will mark the PR ready in ~2 hours after i fold in priya's snippets and samira's link. @ryan pls review then. if no blockers i'll merge and backfill redirects.
ryan: :thumbsup: will review promptly when notified.
elena: putting a checklist in the PR description: update links, add snippets (js/python), embed flow slide, add retry table, link to Optimize for advanced tuning. marking WIP now.
